description: Step 3 of the extern door collapse, cut back by the user to a pure deletion. Today native code replaces a comparison export with an inline compare because RUNTIME_SYMBOLS grants RuntimeNativeBinding::Comparison(RuntimeComparison::LtII ..) to the validated declaration; a 24-variant enum and a 170-line match un-flatten that back into (BinOp, CmpOperands). The grant is keyed on a symbol string in a manifest that is being deleted, and it sits one call too low to save the Kernel clause call anyway. Decision: delete the mechanism outright; every comparison export (fz_op_lt_ii .. fz_op_not_identical) lowers natively as an ordinary C call through lower_extern_generic, exactly as arithmetic already does. Getting the instruction back is fz-5xp.20's general inliner, not a comparison-specific key. Deleted: RuntimeNativeBinding, RuntimeComparison, native_binding column, runtime_binding fields on LoweredExtern/ExternDecl, lower_runtime_comparison, lower_typed_cmp, CmpOperands, emit_mixed_numeric_cmp, the binding check in lower_prim's Prim::Extern arm, and any test asserting a comparison export is not called natively. Proof: fixture matrix on three doors (mixed numeric ordering, binary ordering, == widening, === strict).
title: Delete the manifest's native comparison binding; comparison exports become ordinary C calls
